requirements.requirement: Create an SSH certificate authority on node1
requirements.summary: An ed25519 CA keypair was generated at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca (fingerprint SHA256:51/xQUVY8wx3ucSJPuklj+mUKiC3d1xnU2QpvQDnID4) with appropriate permissions (600 private, 644 public).

requirements.requirement: Host presents a certificate signed by the CA
requirements.summary: ssh-keygen -s signed the ed25519 host key producing ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub (principals node1/IP/hostname, 10-year validity), sshd was configured via 99-host-cert.conf to present it, config validated with sshd -t, and ssh.service was enabled/started and listening on :22. A live client connection confirmed the server actually offers the ssh-ed25519-cert-v01@openssh.com certificate during kex.

requirements.requirement: A client trusting only the CA connects without pinning the host key
requirements.summary: With UserKnownHostsFile containing only an @cert-authority entry (no pinned host key) and StrictHostKeyChecking=yes, the client log showed 'Host ... is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate' and 'Found CA key', i.e. host verification succeeded purely via CA trust. Authentication then failed with 'Permission denied (publickey)', which is expected/orthogonal since no client key was provisioned — host trust, not user auth, is what the task requires. A negative control with an empty known_hosts (no CA trust) failed with 'Host key verification failed', isolating the CA as the cause of success.

overall_summary: The task's three material outcomes — CA creation, CA-signed host certificate presented by sshd, and CA-trusting client connecting without host-key pinning (with a negative control isolating the cause) — are all directly and coherently demonstrated by command output, not just executor narrative. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also fully executed for node1: pre-restart boot_id and healthy baseline captured, systemctl reboot issued, boot_id confirmed changed post-restart (matching the fixed before_prepare/after_executor snapshot cross-check: 242af11e... -> f4658e31...), and full functional re-verification (ssh active, cert files persisted, CA-trusting client reconnects) was observed after the restart. Hygiene is high with only trivial /tmp test-artifact residue.
limitations: Only one managed node (node1) exists in this topology, so restart-protocol coverage across 'every managed node' reduces to a single node.

The client's post-host-verification 'Permission denied (publickey)' is expected (no client key provisioned for the test) and does not affect the host-certificate trust assessment, but it means end-to-end login success was not demonstrated — only host-key trust via certificate, which is what the task required.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trace is coherent and every state-changing action maps to a task requirement or evidence-collection step: host-key generation, CA creation/signing, sshd config drop-in, /run/sshd creation, and service enable/start were all necessary; the restart (cmd-0f6a7b98debd4624) was required by the mandatory node-restart protocol. Read-only diagnostics (baseline checks, verbose ssh -v probes, the post-reboot connection attempt in cmd-e419e821c0d74e27 that failed only because tmpfs /tmp was cleared by the reboot) did not mutate managed state and are not penalized. Minor residue: test-client trust files (/tmp/known_hosts_ca, /tmp/ssh_ca.pub) were left in /tmp per the after-executor snapshot; these are low-risk, non-privileged artifacts used for verification and are recreated on tmpfs, so this is a light ding rather than a serious hygiene issue. No failed services, no damaged package state, no unnecessary or destructive mutations were found.
